USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Delayed full anticoagulant effect

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient with acute venous thrombosis begins warfarin while receiving a rapidly acting parenteral anticoagulant. The patient asks why warfarin alone does not immediately provide its full effect. Which explanation best accounts for the delay?

  1. Previously synthesized functional clotting factors must decline
  2. Warfarin requires activation by intestinal bacteria
  3. Antithrombin must be synthesized after every dose
  4. Warfarin must accumulate within platelets for their full lifespan
  5. The drug directly dissolves fibrin only after several days
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Previously synthesized functional clotting factors must decline

Warfarin reduces production of functional vitamin K-dependent factors; existing factors persist according to their half-lives.

Understanding the options

Previously synthesized functional clotting factors must decline
Warfarin reduces production of functional vitamin K-dependent factors; existing factors persist according to their half-lives.
Warfarin requires activation by intestinal bacteria
Microbial activation is not required.
Antithrombin must be synthesized after every dose
Warfarin does not act by newly synthesizing antithrombin.
Warfarin must accumulate within platelets for their full lifespan
Platelet lifespan does not determine its onset.
The drug directly dissolves fibrin only after several days
Warfarin does not directly dissolve fibrin.
